items.stem: What does optional binding with if let accomplish in Swift?

options.text: It safely unwraps an optional into a non-optional constant when a value exists
options.rationale: if let binds the wrapped value only when the optional is non-nil.

options.text: It forces the optional to a value, crashing if nil
options.rationale: That is force-unwrapping with !, not if let.

options.text: It converts any type into an optional
options.rationale: if let unwraps, it does not wrap.
if let introduces a constant unless if var is used.

items.explanation: if let binds the wrapped value only when the optional is non-nil.

items.stem: Select TWO true statements about structs as value types in Swift.

options.text: Assigning a struct to a new variable copies it
options.rationale: Value types are copied on assignment.

options.text: Mutating the copy does not affect the original
Structs are reference types sharing one instance
options.rationale: Structs are value types, not reference types.

options.text: Two struct variables always point to the same memory
options.rationale: Each copy has its own storage.

items.explanation: Value types are copied on assignment.

items.stem: Why prefer the nil-coalescing operator ?? over force-unwrapping an optional?

options.text: It supplies a fallback value instead of crashing when the optional is nil
options.rationale: ?? yields a default on nil, avoiding a runtime trap.

options.text: It is faster at runtime than any alternative
options.rationale: Performance is not the reason; safety is.

options.text: It converts the value to a String
options.rationale: ?? does not change the type beyond removing optionality.

options.text: It makes the optional non-optional permanently

items.explanation: ?? yields a default on nil, avoiding a runtime trap.
